meta.title: Astragaloi Data Corpus — the 56 casts of the five-knucklebone oracle
meta.assembled: 2026-07-25, for the theourgia platform, from the hellinismos-grimoire notes (transcription only; nothing invented)
meta.mechanics: Five astragaloi (knucklebones); each lands on one of four faces valued 1, 3, 4 or 6 (opposite faces sum to 7; never 2 or 5). 56 distinct unordered combinations; sums run 5–30, with 6 and 29 impossible.

meta.tetraktys_overlay: The Order's own composition (Session 16), NOT attested tradition: sphere = sum mod 10 (0→10); octave = luminous (sum ≤10) / embodied (11–20) / chthonic (21–30); ground_element = the sphere-row's element, Scheme A (locked): 1=Fire, 2–3=Air, 4–6=Water, 7–10=Earth.

verse_policy.verse_greek: Heinevetter text verbatim from oracle-verses-translation.md, diacritics and apparatus markers preserved (including the stone's throw-letter/numeral/god-genitive header line); null where not preserved in Heinevetter's witnesses (awaits Nollé). XI is from Costanza/Nollé, not Heinevetter's witnesses.
verse_policy.verse_english: The Order's draft rendering from the Greek (every 'Final (Sophia)' line was blank at assembly); where the draft is absent or fragmentary, the Graf-derived English of the attested-56 table is used instead and flagged in that cast's notes.

caveats: All translations are drafts pending Sophia's collation of Nollé 2007 (the standard edition); her corrected line is final and none exist yet.

Two provisional throw corrections, to verify against Nollé in print: XXVI (Hermes the Saviour, sum 17) was recorded as 1·6·6·3·4 (=20) and is corrected to 6·4·3·3·1 on sum-consistency grounds; XIII (The Seasons, sum 13) was recorded as 3·3·3·3·1 (a duplicate of XII) and is assigned 4·4·3·1·1 — but Heinevetter's restored throw [ΓΓΓΓ]Α supports the INVERSE assignment (Seasons to 3·3·3·3·1, Zeus & Athena to 4·4·3·1·1). Nollé decides.
XXXVII: the surviving Greek does NOT correspond to Graf's English ('the sun has set…') — must collate.

God-name variants pending collation: VI (Εὐδαίμων vs Φρονίμη), XIX (Ἀγαθή vs Σωτήρ), XXVIII (Τίσις vs Νέμεσις), XXXI (Ἱκέσιος vs Μέγιστος), XXXV (Κερδένπορος vs Κερδῷος), XXXVIII (stone Νεμέσεως vs later Σελήνη), XXXIX (stone Διὸς νεκρῶν κηδεμόνος vs later Διόσκουροι), XLII (stone Ἡλίου Φωσφόρου), XLVI (stone Ἄρεως Θουρίου vs modern Δεινός), XLVIII (stone Εὐφροσύνης vs modern Εὐδαιμονία).
Which broad face is physically 3 vs 4 is uncertain (sources disagree) — the numbers are certain, the face isn't; decide once per bone-set and keep it consistent.
NOT ancient: the popular 'Apollo & Hermes, lead the way' invocation (Opsopaus 1995); and the 'dog = worst / Aphrodite = best' valuation belongs to the four-bone gaming throw, not this oracle.
Valence keys are the Order's calls from Graf's verses; Sophia may re-classify.
The tetraktys overlay (sphere/octave/ground) reflects the Order's map because it was built to — coherence, not attested correspondence.

your setting-out upon the road; the toil bears its fruit;
and good it is to set hand to work, to contest, and to law.
casts.notes: Greek source: (Heinevetter p. 23; T, E, A — the god from E/A; T here mistakenly carries LII's deity). Μηνὸς Φωσφόρου from E and A (T's scribe wandered to LII's goddess). Note Men shares Phosphoros with Helios (XLII) and with Hekate — the light-bearing family across the corpus.

casts.verse_greek:
ϚϚϚϚΑ   ΚΕ   Μητρὸς θεῶν.
τέσσαρες ἐξεῖται, πέμπτος χεῖος, τάδε φράζει·
ὡς ἄρνας κατέχουσι λύκοι κρατεροί τε λέοντε[ς
βοῦς ἕλικας, πάντων οὕτω[ς] (ἔτι) καὶ σὺ κρατήσεις,
(κ)αὶ πάντ᾿ ἔσται σοι ὅσ᾿ ἐρωτᾷς σὺν Διὸς Ἑρ[μῇ.
casts.verse_english:
— Four sixes, and the fifth the dog: this it declares: —
as wolves hold fast the lambs, and mighty lions
the twist-horned oxen, so shall you too master all,
and all that you ask shall be yours — with Hermes, Zeus' own.
casts.notes: Greek source: (Heinevetter p. 24; T, E, A — T mislabels with LI's god). 4) ἔτι from E — H.'s "telling proof" that the reconstruction may fill faulty verses with inserted words. 5) Skutsch reorders. The Homeric simile-pair (wolves/lambs, lions/oxen) is the corpus's grandest figure.

casts.verse_greek:
ϚϚϚΔΔ   (ΚϚ)   Διὸς Καταχθονίου.
τρεῖς (ὁμοῦ) ἐξεῖται, δύο τέσσαρα, χρησμὸς ὅδ᾿ αὐδᾷ·
(ἡ) πρᾶξις κωλύματ᾿ ἔχει, μὴ σπεῦδ᾿, ἀνάμεινο(ν).
(λ)υπηρά τις ὁδὸς καὶ ἀμήχανος οὐδὲ προσικτή·
ὠνεῖσθαι χαλεπὸν καὶ πωλεῖν τι βλάβος ἔσται.
casts.verse_english:
— Three sixes together, two fours: this oracle declares: —
the deed is hedged with hindrances: do not hasten; wait.
A grievous road, past helping, not to be approached;
buying is hard, and to sell will bring some harm.
casts.notes: Greek source: (Heinevetter p. 24; T, E, partly A). Διὸς Καταχθονίου — H. cites Il. 9.457 (Ζεὺς καταχθόνιος) for the title: the book's Subterranean Zeus stands on Homeric ground. 3) T's ἀλλ᾿ purged as unmetrical.

casts.verse_greek:
ϚϚϚϚΓ   ΚΖ   Ἀφροδείτης (Οὐρανίας).
τέσσαρ(ες) ἐξεῖται, μοῦνος τρία σοι τάδε φράζει·
οὐρανόπαις Ἀφροδείτη, Ἐρώτων πότνι᾿ ἄνασσα
πέμψει μαντείαν ἀγαθήν, δώσει δὲ ὁδόν σοι
(ἔ)κφευξ(ίν) τε νόσου καὶ φροντίδος (ἀλγε)σιθύμου.
casts.verse_english:
— Four sixes, and a lone three: this it declares to you: —
Heaven-born Aphrodite, mistress of the Loves, O queen:
she will send a good oracle, and grant you your road,
and escape from sickness, and from heart-grieving care.
casts.notes: Greek source: (Heinevetter p. 25; T and E — COLLATED with Costanza p. 28 / Nollé p. 178: agreement, T's ἐκφεύξῃ = Costanza's text). Οὐρανίας from E. Line 5: E's noun ἔκφευξιν vs T's verb ἐκφεύξῃ (= Costanza/Nollé) — Sophia chooses. ἀλγεσίθυμος previously attested only at Orphic Hymn 65.6 (H.) — with κερδέμπορος (XXXV), the corpus shares rare diction with the Hymns. 3) E: Ἐρώτων πότνια σεμνή, cf. Eur. Phaethon fr. 781.16.

casts.verse_greek:
ϚϚϚϚΔ   ΚΗ   Βλάβης.
τέσσαρες ἐξεῖται καὶ τετρῶος τάδε φράζει·
οὐκ ἔστιν πρᾶξ(ις)· τί μάτην (σπεύδεις; ἀνάμεινον,)
μή σοι σπεύδοντι βλάβος ([ἐξ] αὐτῆς) τι γένηται·
οὔτε γὰρ εἰς ὁδὸν ὁρμᾶσθαι καλὸν οὔτ᾿ ἀγοράζε(ιν).
casts.verse_english:
— Four sixes and a four: this it declares: —
there is no deed here. Why hasten in vain? Wait,
lest to you in your hastening some damage come of it;
for neither is it good to set out upon the road, nor to buy.
casts.notes: Greek source: (Heinevetter p. 25; T, E; scraps in Y, K, O). the goddess's name sounds within her own verse (Βλάβης — βλάβος): nominal omen. 3) ἀλλ᾿ purged for metre as at LIII 3. The stonecutter's ΠΕΙΠΤΟΝΤΟΣΟΠΕΙΠΤΩΝ blunder corrected by Kaibel.

casts.verse_greek:
ϚϚϚϚϚ   (Λ)   Ἑρμοῦ Τετραγώνου.
εἰ δέ κεν ἐξεῖται πάντες πείπτωσιν ὁμοῖοι,
(μ)ὴ βαῖν᾿ ἣν μέλλεις, μείναντί σοι ἔσται ἄμεινον.
(αἰσχρὸν γάρ σοι κ[ῆ]δος ὁρῶ περὶ ὧν μ᾿ ἐπερωτᾷς·)
(ἀλλὰ μέν᾿ ἡσύχιος λήξας ὁδοῦ ἠδ᾿ ἀγορασμοῦ.)
casts.verse_english:
— If all that fall are sixes, all alike: —
go not the way you intend: for the one who waits it shall be better;
for I see a shameful care in what you ask me —
but remain quiet, ceasing from the road and from the market.
casts.notes: Greek source: (Heinevetter p. 26; T and E; scraps in K, Y, O). E's throw-verse variant: πάντες ὁμοῦ ἐξεῖται Φοίβου φωνῆς ἐπάκουσον — "all sixes together: hearken to the voice of Phoibos" — the very formula H. used to restore Oracle I: the corpus's end validates its beginning. T's alternative ending: τόν τε φόβον λύσει καὶ τὸν κάμνοντα δὲ σώσει ("he will loose your fear and save the sick" — whence Graf's close). Lines 4-5 echo XXXVII 4 and XLIV 5: the stone's formulas returning at the summit. The highest throw counsels the deepest stillness.
